Critical Materials, Minerals & Microbial Mechanisms

An evidence-backed knowledge base for critical minerals and materials, connecting strategic commodities and mineral hosts to microbial extraction, biomineralization, and recovery mechanisms.

Curated Processes

Mechanism records describe biological and abiotic processes, with experimental materials, conditions, evidence and limitations. Microbial involvement is stated explicitly.

Bioleaching
185 mechanisms

Microbial solubilization and mobilization of target metals from ores, concentrates, and wastes.

Biomineralization
107 mechanisms

Biological precipitation, crystallization, and synthesis of mineral phases or nanoparticles.

Redox Transformation
61 mechanisms

Oxidation-reduction reactions that alter metal valence states; microbial involvement is specified in each record.

Biosorption
17 mechanisms

Passive binding and retention of metal ions by microbial cell walls and biomass.

Separation
31 mechanisms

Selective partitioning by biological or abiotic processes. See each record for microbial involvement, experimental conditions and recovery limits.

Recovery
19 mechanisms

Integrated microbial processing schemes yielding concentrated or isolated materials.

Other Transformations
186 mechanisms

Complex community transformations, multi-stage processes, or unclassified interactions.

Evidence & Curation Contract

CMMMech records enforce rigorous scientific limits:

Chemical identity separation: An element (e.g. Lithium) is strictly distinct from its mineral hosts (e.g. Spodumene, Jadarite) and its commercial form.
Mechanism evidence boundaries: Laboratory solubilization or binding is explicitly distinguished from full industrial recovery, elemental yield, or isolated pure metal.
Negative & control evidence: Abiotic controls, matched acid baselines, and null results are recorded alongside positive extraction claims to prevent inflated efficacy.
Structured provenance: Records cite their evidence sources and include material or organism identifiers where verified.
